text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Limuru Member of Parliament George Nyanja bars opposition FORD-Asili Secretary-General Martin Shikuku and vice-chairman George Nthenge from using the party's headquarters in Nairobi.
- The Centre for Governance and Development says the political situation in Kenya is "red hot" and might erupt any time.
- Police Commissioner Shedrach Kiruki says torture in whatever form is illegal and dehumanising.
- Business tycoon Amin Alibhai admits escaping from a London prison where he was serving a seven-year jail term but denies he is a fugitive on the run.

- A branch chairman of the ruling party Kenya African National Union (KANU) confirms the existence of two camps in the ruling party and blames it on a clique of top KANU officials including cabinet ministers.
- Fishing industry and foreign distributors say Uganda risks losing a large portion of its $50 million-a-year fish exports if it sprays chemicals on the water hyacinth in Lake Victoria.
